Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a time-ordered data structure with dynamic updates and range Kadane queries, useful for analytics with streaming events.

Key Concepts

- Kadane’s algorithm generalized to segments via a monoid: sum, pref, suff, best.
- Handling duplicates by aggregating per timestamp.
- Range queries using split/merge or traversal to collect O(log n) aggregates.

```javascript
// Pseudocode sketch of node structure and combine(a,b)
class Node{ constructor(t, w){ this.t = t; this.cnt = 1; this.sum = w; this.pref = Math.max(0, w); this.suff = Math.max(0, w); this.best = w; } }
function combine(left, right){ /* merge Kadane aggregates */ }
```

- How would you extend to support deletions by weight and query the exact subarray indices when multiple subarrays tie for best sum?
- How would you adapt for 2D time-series (two timestamps) or streaming without offline compression?
